title: Add offline Helm OCI seeding and precompiled BPF-CNI module bundles for air-gapped kernels
author: Mateo Alvarez
release_notes: Adds support for precompiled BPF CNI bundles and a new offline Helm OCI seeder; improves airgap installer device/kernel compatibility and adds signed bundle verification
description: Motivation: Customers running Redwood Private in fully air-gapped datacenters reported two recurring issues: 1) inconsistent CNI installs when kernels differ from our build matrix, and 2) manual, error-prone steps to seed private OCI/Helm registries. This PR introduces an end-to-end offline-friendly flow: packaged, precompiled BPF-CNI kernel module bundles for common enterprise kernels plus a new OCI-Helm seeder sidecar utility that can be run from the airgap bootstrap container to atomically seed registries and charts. Summary of changes: packaged kernel module artifacts per distro (ubuntu20/22, rhel8/9, rocky, almalinux) with vmlinuz/headers checksums; an installer hook that probes target nodes and selects the closest-compatible module bundle; an offline Helm OCI seeder that pulls from provided artifact tarballs and imports images/charts into the local registry with optional signature verification; terraform module updates to create a registry seed job and a registry credential secret; Helm chart tweaks to surface device-mapper and module-loader knobs; and tests and preflight checks added to the installer preflight. Design notes: To avoid kernel compilation in customer environments we ship prebuilt, signed .ko bundles plus a fingerprint manifest. The installer probes uname -r and glibc/kernel headers and performs a checksum-based compatibility match; if no exact match exists, it falls back to a closest ABI-compatible bundle and inserts a graceful warning in the console output and audit log. The OCI seeder uses an idempotent import layer: tarball->verify->import->promote so retries are safe. Security: all bundles and helm charts are signed with our airgap signing key and verified locally before install; signature failure aborts the seeding step and surfaces a clear remediation path. Migration and rollout: added a canary flag in the installer config (installer.canary.offline_module_loader=true) to enable gradual rollout on Dedicated/Private installs. For major customer migrations we provide a helper script that collects /lib/modules and system info to help produce a custom bundle. Testing: added unit tests for the module selector logic, integration test harness that runs the seeder against a local registry in CI (recorded in ci/seeder-e2e), and manual validation on Ubuntu 20.04 kernel variants. CI run notes: initial CI run failed linter on variable naming in terraform module; fixed in second commit and all checks passed. Backwards compatibility: the default remains the previous build-from-source flow unless the canary flag is set. Documentation: added docs/private/offline-seeding.md and a troubleshooting section for kernel mismatches. Rollout plan: merge to main, cut a 0.31.0-alpha private-installer image with seeder sidecar, enable canary for internal staging clusters, gather telemetry on module fallback events before broad rollout. Related: ENG-12458 tracks broader vendor bundle matrix expansion.

review_comments: Priya Kapoor: Please add a clear audit log entry when the installer falls back to a non-exact kernel bundle. We need this for support triage.

Mateo Alvarez: Added an audit log line and included it in the doc troubleshooting steps (see docs/private/offline-seeding.md). Also added a telemetry tag 'module_fallback' to the installer heartbeats.
Ethan Ross: Terraform change looks good but we should add an expiration TTL on the registry seed job to avoid orphaned jobs.
Mateo Alvarez: Added ttl_seconds_after_finished to the Job spec and moved credentials to a k8s secret with limited RBAC scope.
Lena Müller: One security question: where is the signing key stored for airgap customers? We need to document the rotation pattern.
Mateo Alvarez: Documented recommended customer flow: use their KMS to sign bundles or request a signed bundle from Redwood; rotation guidance added in docs and an 'unbind' helper to revoke a bundle.

merge_commit: 9f1a3bd: squash merge of offline seeder and module bundles
notes_for_support: If customers see 'module_fallback' events, advise collecting /var/log/redwood/installer.log and output of uname -r and /lib/modules; recommend requesting a custom bundle via support with the collected manifest. If signature verification fails, check that the provided signing key matches the bundle fingerprint and that network time is synced for validity window checks.
changelog_entry: Private-installer: Add offline OCI-Helm seeder, precompiled BPF-CNI kernel bundles, installer probes for kernel compatibility, and signed bundle verification. (canary behind installer.canary.offline_module_loader)
notes: This PR focuses on air-gapped reliability; follow-up work (ENG-12458) will expand the kernel matrix and add an automated bundle builder pipeline.
